metadata.title: BlackRock Kicks Off $12.3 Billion Bond Sale for Meta Data Center

content.text:
(Bloomberg) -- BlackRock Inc. began marketing $12.3 billion of high-grade bonds to fund a Meta Platforms Inc. data center project, testing investor appetite amid growing concerns about excessive AI infrastructure spending.

Sopaipilla Investor, a holding company tied to BlackRock, is offering a single tranche of notes due in 2048, according to a person familiar with the matter. Price talk is a premium of about 2.875 percentage points over Treasuries, the person said, asking not to be identified because they aren't authorized to speak publicly.
Proceeds from the sale will fund a data center campus in El Paso, Texas, expected to provide as much as 1 gigawatt of computing capacity for artificial intelligence workloads. BlackRock subsidiaries Global Infrastructure Management and HPS Investment Partners hold an 80% stake in the project, with Meta owning the remaining 20%.
JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Morgan Stanley are running the offering.
